question.problem:
A factory produces shovels, each consisting of a handle and a blade.
The length of a handle is normally distributed with a mean of $120$ centimeters and a variance of $0.14,$  while the length of a blade is normally distributed with a mean of $30$ centimeters and a variance of $0.02.$ If one shovel is randomly selected, what is the probability that its length is more than $150$ centimeters, but less than $150.5$ centimeters? You may assume that the lengths are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8944\,$ | $\,0.8962\,$ | $\,0.8980\,$ | $\,0.8997\,$ | $\,0.9015\,$ |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9115\,$ | $\,0.9131\,$ | $\,0.9147\,$ | $\,0.9162\,$ | $\,0.9177\,$ |
| $\,1.4\,$ | $\,0.9265\,$ | $\,0.9279\,$ | $\,0.9292\,$ | $\,0.9306\,$ | $\,0.9319\,$ |
